unmatched.body:
First, thanks for stepping up and assisting. This is all for
Xai/Southhaven, MS.

PDF visuals explaining why this is happening are attached, FOIA's Zipped in
PDF format, ready for signing. I want the city workers to see why we are
bringing these requests hopefully open someones eyes who can get more
internal documents, ie procure a whistleblower.

Xai paid off a few officials and donated to some campaigns in exchange for
a $100 million-a-year tax break and its facilities create a public nuisance
with the added potential to harm our water table, which is my main
concern.


Send this to kpearson@southaven.org + certified mail with receipt

*Letter 1 — MDEQ*
Public Records Officer
Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality
P.O. Box 2261
Jackson, MS 39225

*Letter 2 — City of Southaven* (the one matching the email to the clerk)
City Clerk
City of Southaven
8710 Northwest Drive
Southaven, MS 38671

*Letter 3 — MDA*
Public Records Officer
Mississippi Development Authority
P.O. Box 849
Jackson, MS 39205-0849

*Letter 4 — Campaign finance (county officials)*
Circuit Clerk
DeSoto County Courthouse
2535 Highway 51 South
Hernando, MS 38632
*Companions: City Clerk (same Southaven address above) for the
mayor/aldermen reports, and MS Secretary of State, Elections Division, P.O.
Box 136, Jackson, MS 39205.*

*Letter 5 — Assessor / Collector*
DeSoto County Tax Assessor / Tax Collector
365 Losher Street, Suites 100 & 110
Hernando, MS 38632






















*Dear Ms. Pearson,Pursuant to the Mississippi Public Records Act (Miss.
Code Ann. § 25-61-1 et seq.), please find attached a public records request
submitted on behalf of the Move Weight Foundation, dated July 28, 2026.In
summary, the request seeks Board of Aldermen agendas, minutes, resolutions,
and related records concerning: (1) the December 23, 2025 Memorandum of
Understanding with MZX Tech, LLC ($3,460,000 for road improvements); (2)
the December 29, 2025 Musk Foundation Grant Agreement ($1,850,000); (3) the
Donation Agreement with MZX Tech LLC ($1,380,900 for the Southaven Police
Department); and (4) the Ad Valorem Tax (Fee-in-Lieu) Agreement executed
January 2026 — together with records of receipt and expenditure of those
funds and related legal correspondence. The full request is set out in the
attached letter.We request copies rather than inspection, with electronic
delivery (email or download link) preferred. If any portion of the request
is withheld or redacted, please identify each record withheld and cite the
specific statutory exemption relied upon. If estimated fees will exceed
$25.00, please contact me with an estimate before fulfillment.Please
confirm receipt of this request by reply email. We understand that Miss.
Code Ann. § 25-61-5 provides seven (7) working days for a response from
receipt.If it is the City's preference that this request also be submitted
on the City of Southaven Public Record Request form, please let me know and
we will promptly return a completed form; in the meantime, please treat
this email and attachment as the operative request as of the date
received.Thank you for your assistance.Sincerely,Wade IvyMove Weight
Foundation1028 I St NWMiami, OK 74354Foia@moveweight.com
<Foia@moveweight.com> | 310-658-6281*




-- 
Thank You,
Austin Sherman

unmatched.subject: [Tip f4662dca0d] Other
unmatched.body:
New tip via ExposeSanAngelo.com
========================================

Tip ID  : f4662dca0d
Received: 2026-09-07T02:34:11Z
Topic   : Other
Contact : (anonymous — none given)

Message
----------------------------------------
**Possible story: Midland Health pressures nurses to earn bachelor’s degrees while senior leadership is not held to the same educational standard**

I believe Midland Health has an education and leadership double standard that deserves investigation.

Midland Health publicly states that it wants 80% of its nursing staff to hold a BSN. Nurses are strongly encouraged to go back to school and obtain bachelor's degrees so the hospital can improve this organizational metric.

The question employees are asking is: **Why are frontline nurses being pushed so hard to obtain additional formal education when some of the highly compensated senior leaders above them are not held to comparable educational or professional standards?**

These are nurses working 12-hour shifts, taking care of patients, dealing with staffing issues, burnout and family responsibilities. Publicly reported salary information currently places many Midland Memorial registered nurses around $74,000–$93,000 per year, with BSN RNs around $80,000–$100,000.

Now compare the burden being placed on those employees with senior leadership.

Midland Health has numerous vice presidents and senior executives whose compensation should be obtainable through public-records requests because Midland County Hospital District is a governmental hospital district. I believe a reporter should obtain the current salaries of the vice presidents and compare them directly with the salaries of the nurses being pressured to return to school.

The disparity is not simply about money. It is about standards.

Some senior leaders have responsibility over healthcare operations and even clinical practices despite not having clinical educational backgrounds comparable to the employees they oversee. For example, Midland Health's own biography states that its Vice President of Community Health oversees Midland Health-affiliated physician practices. Her published educational background is a bachelor's degree in Mass Communications and an MBA.

Yet frontline nurses—people who already hold nursing licenses, provide direct patient care and carry enormous clinical responsibility—are the employees being pushed to obtain an additional bachelor's degree.

I have also personally observed a senior leader with responsibility involving clinical practices struggle with basic terminology and acronyms commonly used in healthcare quality. I am intentionally not describing the exact meeting or circumstances because doing so could identify me. However, this is something that could be independently investigated by interviewing current and former employees.

This is not an argument against nurses obtaining bachelor's degrees. Education is valuable.

The issue is **whether Midland Health practices what it preaches.**

If bachelor's-level education is considered so important that the hospital has established an organizational goal of getting 80% of its nurses to a BSN, why isn't there an equally visible push requiring senior leaders to obtain education directly related to the clinical, quality or operational areas they oversee?

Why should an RN earning roughly $75,000–$100,000 per year, working long shifts and caring directly for patients, be pressured to spend evenings and weekends completing another degree so the hospital can improve an institutional metric, while an executive earning substantially more may face no comparable requirement to obtain additional education related to the area that executive oversees?

I believe a reporter should request and compare:

• Current salaries and total compensation for Midland Health vice presidents and senior executives.

• Current RN and BSN-RN salaries.

• Educational requirements for every vice-president position.

• The actual educational credentials of individuals currently occupying those positions.

• Which executives have responsibility over clinical practices, quality, patient safety and nursing-related operations.

• Midland Health communications to nurses regarding its 80% BSN objective.

• Whether nurses are formally or informally pressured to obtain BSNs and whether education affects advancement opportunities.

• Whether senior executives are similarly required to obtain additional degrees or professional credentials after assuming responsibility for specialized areas.

• Employee turnover, vacancy, burnout and nursing retention data.

This could answer a simple but important question:

**Does Midland Health demand educational advancement primarily from the employees providing bedside care, while allowing the highest-paid people in the organization to operate under a different standard?**

I am submitting this anonymously because employees may fear professional retaliation for publicly questioning senior leadership. I encourag

unmatched.subject: Engineer interested in contributing to ExposeMississippi
unmatched.body:
Hi Move Weight team!

I'm Lex and I recently came across ExposeMississippi while researching
public meetings and civic data infrastructure in the Jackson area.

I'm a senior software engineer with over 10 years of experience. I've
worked at Ticketmaster, TaskRabbit, Rhino, and several startups, building
systems serving millions of users. I'm also an active open-source
contributor, with contributions to projects that support the global
developer ecosystem like pnpm and webpack.

I've been exploring ways to contribute my engineering experience to
organizations working on public-interest technology in Mississippi.

Your work caught my attention because I've been thinking about many of the
same problems: collecting government records, normalizing public meeting
data, making documents searchable, and using machine learning to help
people investigate large collections of information.

I'd be interested in contributing to your existing infrastructure, whether
that's building data ingestion pipelines, developing APIs, improving
document search, or tackling a technical problem your team hasn't had the
resources to address.

I'm spending time in the Jackson area and have some availability over the
next few weeks.

Would someone on your team be open to a brief conversation about your
technical needs?

Best,
Lex

unmatched.subject: Non-Profit 501c3 FOIA Requests
unmatched.body:
Dear Ms. Moore,

My name is Wade Ivy. I am the founder and director of the Move Weight 
Foundation, a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. I am writing to 
formally introduce our foundation and its first sponsored organization: 
Expose Miami Oklahoma (exposemiamiok.com), a citizen transparency 
project focused on government accountability in Miami and Ottawa County.

Over the past weeks, Move Weight Foundation has submitted several Open 
Records requests to the City of Miami. We have since been informed that 
the City's legal department, as of April 2026, no longer accepts records 
requests by email. We respect this policy and are submitting all 
requests in the City's official format going forward, with this email 
serving as our formal introduction and cover letter.

Below is a summary of the requests we have previously submitted, along 
with the corresponding completed Open Records Request Forms. We ask that 
these be processed together as our foundation's initial transparency 
audit of Miami city government.

Previously Submitted Requests - These will be in-person handed tomorrow:

Request #1 — 4b137b924aa9e322 City Council Meeting Minutes & Resolutions 
(January 2026 – Present) Including any executive session records.

Request #2 — d8b1e611982d3d2d City Social Media Records (All Platforms) 
Complete content and activity logs for all City of Miami social media 
accounts — Facebook (miamiokla, miamiokpd, miamiokmainstreet, and all 
departmental pages), Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, and any other 
platforms. Including hidden, deleted, or restricted-visibility content, 
administrator lists, and content moderation logs. The City's social 
media policy is also requested.

Request #3 — ad40efc713323c4f Animal Control Policies, Procedures & 
Incident Records Standard operating procedures, after-hours response 
protocols, Police Department coordination policies, incident reports for 
1020 I Street NW area (January 2024–present), all dog bite/attack 
incidents citywide (January 2024–present), staffing levels, budget, and 
overtime records for FY 2025–2026, and shelter intake/outcome records 
for the past 24 months.

Request #4 — 03ec461c984898f8 City Attorney Employment Records — Misty 
Barnes Employment contract, position description, compensation, 
performance evaluations, disciplinary records (January 2023–present), 
all District Attorney referrals regarding citizen complaints (January 
2024–present), and any records regarding handling of photographs 
involving minors by the City Attorney's office.

Request #5 — e9a65a7426368454 Complete Digital Export — All City Social 
Media Accounts Full export of all City-operated social media content 
from Facebook, Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, and other platforms. The 
Foundation is prepared to provide a USB drive for data transfer at no 
cost to the City.

Request #6 — c20aeee42d59b110 Communications Between Council Member Kyla 
Jones & Mayor Bless Parker All emails, text messages, and electronic 
communications between Council Member Jones and Mayor Parker from 
January 2025 through June 2026.

Going forward, all official Open Records correspondence from the Move 
Weight Foundation will be sent from foia@moveweight.com. We respectfully 
request that this email address be retained in your records as the 
primary point of contact for all Foundation records requests. In 
addition to electronic submission, we will deliver printed copies of all 
requests in person or by mail to ensure compliance with the City's 
current submission policy.

The Foundation is prepared to pay reasonable fees for record retrieval 
and copying as authorized under 51 O.S. § 24A.5. Should any request be 
denied in whole or in part, we ask that you identify each record 
withheld, the specific statutory exemption, and the name of the person 
authorizing the denial per 51 O.S. § 24A.7.

I can be reached at 310-658-6281 or by mail at: Move Weight Foundation 
1028 I Street NW Miami, Oklahoma 74354

Respectfully submitted,

Wade Ivy - Move Weight Foundation foia@moveweight.com | 310-658-6281 
exposemiamiok.com

Move Weight Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. Expose 
Miami Oklahoma is the Foundation's first sponsorship, dedicated to 
government accountability in Miami and Ottawa County, Oklahoma.

unmatched.subject: Formal Objection – Proposed Multi-Unit Development at 1834 A St NE
unmatched.body:
Dear Miami City Clerk and Members of the Miami City Council,

Please accept the attached Formal Letter of Objection concerning the 
proposed redevelopment and conversion of the property located at 1834 A 
St NE, Miami, Oklahoma, into a 4-, 8-, or 12-unit residential complex.

I am submitting this correspondence for consideration by the City 
Council and for inclusion in the official record relating to any 
rezoning request, conditional-use permit, variance, development 
application, building permit, or other City action concerning this property.

The attached letter outlines several significant concerns regarding the 
proposed development, including floodplain and drainage impacts, water 
and sewer capacity, stormwater runoff, electrical infrastructure, 
building and fire-code compliance, environmental testing, parking, 
neighborhood compatibility, and the potential implications of changing 
the property's existing zoning classification.

Given the potential impact on the surrounding Castle Park Addition 
neighborhood, I respectfully ask that the City carefully review these 
issues before granting any approval associated with the proposed 
development.

Please:

 1. Confirm receipt of this email and attachment.
 2. Provide a copy to each member of the Miami City Council.
 3. Include this correspondence in the official record for any current
    or future proceeding concerning 1834 A St NE.
 4. Include it with the relevant Council or planning/zoning agenda
    materials if this property is scheduled for consideration.
 5. Notify me of the date, time, and location of any public meeting,
    hearing, or Council action concerning this proposed development.

Thank you for ensuring that the concerns of the surrounding neighborhood 
are formally documented and considered before any decision is made.

Respectfully,

Wade Ivy

Attachment: Formal Letter of Objection – Proposed Multi-Unit Complex 
Conversion at 1834 A St NE
